checks.claim: C1: The object and labels are exact. White case d=alpha=1, Gamma=delta0, theta=1. Split (1,3): vertex 0 is the singleton, vertices 1<2<3 form the long chain, pair 03 is cross (lambda) and pair 12 is self (nu). The Green product G_u(X)G_v(Y)G_w(0)G_z(X-Y) and the cross delay |u-v-w-z| match this diagram. The mirror (3,1) 01|23 needs the parameters swapped.
checks.reason: Independently checked. The singleton sits at physical time u and position X. The long chain has vertex 1 at (v,Y), vertex 2 at (v+w, x2) and vertex 3 at (v+w+z, x3). The white pairing 12 forces x2=Y, which gives the gap factor G_w(0)=1/2. The pairing 03 forces x3=X, which gives G_z(X-Y). The cross time difference is |u-(v+w+z)| and the self time difference is w, so the damping factors are exp(-lambda|u-v-w-z|) and exp(-nu w), as written. In the mirror, the long chain 0,1,2 comes first and the singleton is 3. The self pair (first two long-chain vertices) is 01 and the cross pair (last long-chain vertex with the singleton) is 23. So canonical pair 01 carries nu and pair 23 carries lambda, which is the stated swap. The fractional weight is symmetric, so the averaged result transfers. The note says explicitly that the transforms are auxiliary chain-gap transforms, not unequal-time correlations or diagonal-horizon coefficients.

checks.claim: C2: The physical rational formula I=N/[32c^3(b+c-1)(b+1)], with N=b(c^2+c+1)+c^3+c+1, c=1+lambda and b=1+nu.
checks.reason: Re-derived every step. (1) In p=v+Y, q=v-Y the constraints |Y|<v and |X-Y|<L-v become 0<p<L+X and 0<q<L-X. The Jacobian is 1/2 and the two Green factors give 1/4, so the convolution is (L^2-X^2)_+/8. (2) Integrating against G_u(X)=1/2 on |X|<m and including G_w(0)=1/2 gives V=(L^2 m - m^3/3)/16. (3) With R=u+L, q=u-L (Jacobian 1/2): for q>=0, m=L and V=(R-q)^3/192, so (1/2)·6e^{-q}/192 = e^{-q}/64. For q=-d<0, R=d+t, m=t/2, L=d+t/2 and V = d^2t/32 + dt^2/32 + t^3/192. The Gamma moments 1, 2 and 6 give e^{-d}(d+1)^2/64. (4) The q<0 part contributes [1/(b+lambda)][1/c+2/c^2+2/c^3]. The q>=0 part splits into q>w, giving 1/(c(b+1)), and q<w, giving 1/((b+lambda)(b+1)). (5) Over the common denominator c^3(b+c-1)(b+1) the numerator is c^2(b+2c-1)+(c^2+2c+2)(b+1) = 2N. So 64I = 2N/[c^3(b+c-1)(b+1)]. No delay, binomial, factorial or half-factor is lost. All integrands are nonnegative (Tonelli), and at lambda=0, I=3/(32b).

For A<s, (C,D,r,R)=(4s^2/[(s-A)(s+A)^2], 2A/[(s-A)(s+A)], A, s). For s<A, (C,D,r,R)=(2A/[(A-s)(A+s)], 4s^2/[(A-s)(A+s)^2], s, A). The bound is used pointwise in s and only nonnegative envelopes are integrated, so the signed C and D are never integrated across s=A. Also 2k=A/(A+1)=(c^2-1)/(c^2+1), and ∫h e^{-d^2w/2}=1/d. So J+ <= F0/[64 sqrt(b^2+2k)] = P/[16c^3(c+1)sqrt(b^2+(c^2-1)/(c^2+1))].
